sections.h2: Who records deeds in Sanilac County, Michigan?
sections.html:
Every paper that changes or burdens title to land in this county ends up at the Register of Deeds office in Sandusky. Deeds, mortgages, land contracts, easements, liens, plats, surveys and court orders about real estate all get indexed there, and the county's own description says the office follows a uniform statewide system with fees set by the legislature.

Drafting is outside its job. The staff will not write a deed or advise on one, so a seller who needs a document prepared should talk to an attorney or a title company first. Once a document exists, the office answers practical questions at (810) 648-2313, and the county's department page links to forms, fee schedules and requirements.

A weekly land transfer list is posted on the same site, naming the parties and the section and township for each deed that cleared that week. With about 963 square miles of land, more than any other Lower Peninsula county, those sections range from farm acreage in the Thumb to cottages near the Lake Huron shore.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record a deed in Sanilac County?
sections.html:
A deed costs $30 to record here, and the two transfer taxes add $8.60 for each $1,000 of price. The county's fee schedule spells out the rest, and the table gathers the amounts a seller meets most often.

What the Sanilac County fee schedule charges around a sale
ItemAmountAuthority
Entering and recording one document$30, any page countMCL 600.2567(1)(a)
Added to that for each extra instrument assigned or discharged$3MCL 600.2567(1)(b)
Treasurer's tax certificate$5County fee schedule
County transfer tax$1.10 per $1,000MCL 207.504
State transfer tax$7.50 per $1,000MCL 207.525
Copies of recorded real estate documents$1 a page, $5 certificationCounty fee schedule

Work it through for a $160,000 house: 160 thousands at $8.60 is $1,376 in transfer tax. With the recording fee and the certificate, $1,411 goes to government offices before any title company charges.

sections.h2: Who pays the transfer tax on a Sanilac County sale?
sections.html:
The seller carries it. Under the state act the grantor owes the tax, and the statute sets a 15 day clock from delivery of the deed for paying the county treasurer. At the Sanilac counter the tax is simply collected when the deed goes on record.

The deed has to show the full value of the land, or an affidavit giving that value must travel with it. If a sale bundles a house with furniture or equipment, state those values separately and only the real estate is taxed.

Some deeds owe nothing. The state act exempts, among others:

  • a transfer for under $100;
  • a gift deed from a parent to a son or daughter, or from a grandparent to a grandchild;
  • a deed that carries out a court order with no stated price;
  • a deed handed over in foreclosure of a loan backed by a government agency;
  • a land contract, until title actually passes to the buyer.

The county's own act is narrower and leaves out the family gift exemption, so a parent-to-child deed can escape the state portion while still owing the county portion. Name the exemption statute on the deed, because a deed with no price and no exemption comes back.

sections.h2: What must a deed look like to be accepted for recording?
sections.html:
Michigan's recording act, MCL 565.201, lists what a register must see before accepting an instrument, and the county reposts that text on its real estate information page. The main checkpoints:

  • Signatures are in black or dark blue ink, with each name printed below and matching the notary's acknowledgment.
  • The notary's printed name sits close to the notary signature.
  • Grantee addresses and the drafter's name and business address are on the instrument.
  • Sheets run 8.5 by 11 or 8.5 by 14 inches, in at least 10-point type, on white 20-pound paper.
  • A 2.5 inch clear band tops page one, other margins are half an inch, and the first printed line names the kind of recordable event.
  • Any Social Security number loses its first five digits, and foreign-language text carries an English translation.

An instrument that clears those checks cannot be turned away over what it says. One that misses a check is returned unrecorded, and a closing waits.

sections.h2: Does a Sanilac County deed need a tax certificate?
sections.html:
A warranty deed does. The county treasurer certifies the tax status first, at a $5 charge, and the same goes for land contracts, assignments of land contracts and any deed that carries a covenant of warranty.

The fee schedule does not extend that requirement to a plain quit claim deed. A quit claim passes whatever interest the grantor has with no promise about title, which suits a transfer between relatives or an estate cleanup but gives a paying buyer little protection. Buyers who pay market price normally insist on a warranty deed.

Census data for 2020 to 2024 put the middle owner-occupied home in Sanilac County at $168,300. State and county tax on a sale at that figure is about $1,450, so subtract it when comparing what different buyers would leave you with.

sections.h2: How do I pay and where do I find recorded documents?
sections.html:
Cash, checks, money orders and cards all work, with checks written to the Sanilac County Register of Deeds. A card used at the counter requires photo ID, and an online payment location handles register of deeds fees for people who pay remotely.

Searching costs nothing at rod.sanilaccounty.net, where guest users can look through an index that begins in 1801. Page images come as PDFs at $1 a page, with a $5 charge on every order.

Owners can also enroll for the free property fraud alert. Once a parcel is enrolled, any new recording against it triggers a notice to the owner. For farmland or a seasonal cabin that goes unvisited for weeks, that is an inexpensive way to catch a forged deed early.

sections.h2: What is Sanilac County like for sellers?
sections.html:
The county lies along Lake Huron in the Thumb, bordered by Huron County on the north, Tuscola on the west, Lapeer to the southwest and St. Clair on the south. It became an organized county in 1849, counted 40,611 people in 2020, and the Census Bureau's 2025 estimate is 40,083.

Sandusky, Croswell, Marlette and Brown City are the four cities. Lexington, Port Sanilac and Carsonville draw seasonal visitors. State routes M-19, M-25, M-46, M-53, M-81 and M-90 cross the county, and flat, fertile land keeps agriculture central to many parcels.

  • Homes lived in by their owners: 82.6 percent.
  • Typical monthly owner cost with a mortgage: $1,226.
  • Typical gross rent: $807.
  • Household income at the midpoint: $58,863.
  • Building permits issued in 2025: 74.

Buyers tend to be local families or people shopping for a lake place, and an inland house on a township road reaches a different audience than a cottage on the shoreline.

faqs.q: What is the recording charge for a Sanilac County deed?
faqs.a: It is $30 for each document, whatever the length, set by MCL 600.2567. An instrument that assigns or discharges several others adds $3 per extra one.

faqs.q: What combined transfer tax rate applies in Sanilac County?
faqs.a: The rate is $8.60 per $1,000, split into $7.50 for the state and $1.10 for the county. A $200,000 sale generates $1,720, paid by the seller.

faqs.q: Can a deed be mailed to the Sanilac County recorder?
faqs.a: Phone (810) 648-2313 first to confirm the exact total for recording, tax and any certificate. A deed that falls short of MCL 565.201 is sent back without being recorded.

faqs.q: Does the treasurer have to certify my deed first?
faqs.a: Yes for a warranty deed or land contract. The treasurer's certificate costs $5, and the certified deed then goes to the Register of Deeds.

faqs.q: Do gifts to children owe transfer tax in Sanilac County?
faqs.a: A deed from a parent to a child, stepchild or adopted child avoids the state tax, and so does one from a grandparent to a grandchild. The county tax law has no matching exemption, so check your deed with the office before recording.
